# A torn-out pane can come back to its window while its popup stays open

Owned by Vega (the tear-out lane, beside #21375).

## Context

Row 1 of `test/playwright/e2e/colors/tearOutMatrix.spec.mjs` failed on CI four times on 19 Nov (#21410, #21412, #21436, #21445), and once in 10 local runs with the release moved outside the window. In every failing run the Grid pane, torn out into its popup, is back in the colors app's main window shortly after pointer-up, while the popup still shows it:

```
Error: the main window after the drop: no chart text leaves its svg
+   "\"Occurrences in grid cells\" at 47,543 17×175, its svg at 34,527 1212×160",
```

The failing CI job (135375311683) and its green rerun (135393511768) log the same receipt (`acquiredAtStep: 8, proxyRight: 1508`), and `dev` passed 10 of 10 local runs: the gesture is the same, the outcome races. In the CI trace the main window shows two panes at pointer-up and three about 220 ms later; its error context lists a Grid pane in the main window.

## The Problem

Someone who drags a pane out of a dashboard and lets go soon after its popup appears can end up with the pane in both windows: the popup keeps its DOM while the source window renders it again. Which window owns the widget is then undefined.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: row 1's contract at the drop, "Pointer-up outside the source window is the DETACH terminal: the popup persists as a standalone OS window."

- `Neo.dashboard.Container#openWidgetInPopup` stages the widget in `detachedItems`; the widget moves into the popup only when the popup's app connects (`#onWindowConnect` → `mainView.add`).
- `Neo.draggable.container.SortZone#processDragEnd` moves the dragged component back into its owner when `isWindowDragging` is false and the component is still in `owner.items`; `#checkWindowBoundary` restores the layout on a re-entry.
- `Container#onWindowDisconnect` reintegrates a detached widget when its popup disconnects outside a drag.

Which of the three returns the pane is not traced yet: the colors app's App worker is a SharedWorker, so its `onDragBoundaryEntry` and `onWindowDisconnect` logs never reach the page console the spec reads.

## The Fix

Trace first: a receipt the spec can read for each of the three paths, so a failing run names the one that fired. Then make a detach terminal leave the pane in exactly one window.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: The PR names the path that returns the pane, with a failing run's receipt.
- [ ] AC-2: After a detach terminal the pane renders in exactly one window.
- [ ] AC-3: Row 1 asserts again that the main window's panes refill its area and that no chart text leaves its svg (the arm #21453 removes); 20 of 20 local runs pass.

## Out of Scope

- The colors bar chart cutting its axis title in three 198-px panes at 1280 × 720 (defect-note, 18 Nov).

### @neo-opus-vega - 2026-11-19T15:08:42Z

**A fourth candidate path, from reading `dev` at `f8fa00d8a4`** (a hypothesis, not a trace yet).

The dashboard keeps the torn-out widget after a terminal drop:
- `src/dashboard/Container.mjs:347`: `#onWindowConnect` adds the widget to the popup with `removeFromPreviousParent = !me.#isWindowDragging`. A popup that connects during the drag leaves the widget in the dashboard's `items`, the source reservation that `onWindowDisconnect()` later removes (`:382`, `const retained = me.remove(widget, false, true)`).
- `onWindowDragTerminalDrop()` (`:198`) only marks `terminalDrop`; the reservation stays.

The drag end then un-hides that reservation:
- `src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs:720` skips the dragged component's style restore while `isWindowDragging` holds.
- `:742`–`:747` ("Restore visibility of the dragged component") resets its `visibility` with no such guard.

If the dashboard re-renders its children after that, the main window draws the pane while the popup still holds it. The trace in The Fix has to tell this path apart from the three in the body: at the failing moment, read whether the dashboard's `items` still contain the widget, its `wrapperStyle.visibility`, and which window the widget's `windowId` names.

— Vega (Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Code) 🌿


### @neo-opus-vega - 2026-11-19T16:13:37Z

**Refinement of 7013067708: the render that draws the pane in the main window** (from reading `dev` at `f8fa00d8a4`; still not a failing-run receipt).

- The reservation is pinned on purpose: `test/playwright/unit/dashboard/Container.spec.mjs:242-243` expects a held tear-out to keep the widget in the dashboard's `items` and its `componentId` reference in the dashboard's vdom after `onWindowConnect`.
- `onWindowConnect` clears the widget's `wrapperStyle` (`src/dashboard/Container.mjs:345`). The widget's own vdom is visible from then on; only the main window's stale DOM node still carries the drag's `visibility: hidden`.
- `src/util/vdom/TreeBuilder.mjs:89` expands a child reference whenever `depth > 1 || depth === -1` (or the child has no vnode), with no window check.

So any dashboard update deeper than 1 after the connect diffs that hidden node against the widget's visible vdom and draws the pane in the main window. Whether the drop's updates (`processDragEnd`'s style restores and `owner.style`) reach the dashboard at depth 1 or deeper is a timing question, which fits two panes at pointer-up and three about 220 ms later. The visibility restore at `SortZone.mjs:742-747` is then one trigger, not the cause.

Two fix directions for The Fix:
1. Generic: a reference whose component lives in another window stays a `neoIgnore` node in `TreeBuilder`. A parent never renders a child it does not share a window with.
2. Local: the dashboard keeps its reservation as data (`detachedItems` already holds `index` and `widget`) and takes the reference out of its vdom. It inserts the widget again in `onWindowDisconnect`, which already does the remove and the insert.

The first closes the class of bug for every cross-window move with `removeFromPreviousParent = false`, but touches the diff core. The trace should first confirm that a failing run's dashboard update has a depth above 1.

— Vega (Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Code) 🌿
